# The Protagonist

Enfys Livia (D-0132, D-0134). A woman; the mentor-figure of the pseudo-family; the
not-quite-human heart of the story.

## The name

> status: ratified (D-0132, D-0134)

Her name is Enfys Livia (D-0134): a native Welsh given against a Roman-feminine-gens
family name — the bastard half-blood structure (D-0109) worn openly, the mismatch
legible in one breath. The family name carries the imperial side; which parent, and
under what circumstances, remains open prose.

## The Moses arc

> status: ratified (D-0060, D-0071)

She was born outside the empire and adopted — taken — into it: a foot in both worlds.
Raised inside the ruling class, trained in its arts, she eventually rebels; and her
rebellion is a return to a deeper identity and a rejection of a less valid upper-class
value system. That double belonging is the engine of her characterization: she knows
the enemy's grammar from the inside, and must re-learn her own people's from the
outside.

### Parentage

> status: ratified (D-0109)

The double belonging is in her blood, not only her biography: she is a bastard child,
half of one society and half of another, and her name carries it — a given name and a
family name that probably do not match, drawn from different registers. Which two
societies, which side supplied which name, and the circumstances of her parentage
remain open (Q-0010).

## The Archive

> status: ratified (D-0068)

Her depth does not come from long life — immortality was explicitly rejected as the
device (D-0067 below). It comes from having absorbed whole personalities and their
knowledge — other people, perhaps spirits — leaving her with a rich, complicated,
conflicted internal state: a superpower with real costs. She is, by the author's
design, "a different sort of not quite human thing due to the accumulation of
knowledge and personalities" (D-0082), while remaining utterly plausible in behavior.

### Working mechanics of the Archive

> status: provisional (D-0072)

The session's model, approved directionally: the empire used its stolen children as
vessels — forcing the dying minds of captured elders, weavers, and hedge-scholars into
young carriers to harvest their knowledge (the darkest use of the Tithe of Minds).
The absorbed do not dissolve: they persist as a chorus she must govern. Her signature
calm is a discipline — the firewall that keeps a parliament of the dead from
overwhelming one nervous system. Overreach frays it: accents slip, other people's
gestures surface in her hands, and the cost is paid in blood-pressure and memory.
Her defection began when what the empire made her swallow started talking back.

### The Archive is specific, never symbolic

> status: ratified (D-0150, D-0165)

The parliament is curated by circumstance, not representative: specific people,
each there for a specific reason — which harvest, which sweep, which dying elder
the empire forced into her. She is not an omnibus of humanity. In particular, none
of Geir's dead are among them (D-0150): the parent-ghost thread below stays the
only mind tied to a companion, and that uniqueness is load-bearing.

And the parliament is audible one voice at a time (D-0165): the minds she carries
are individually distinct and mostly less muddled than her blended surface. When a
specific mind rises in her speech it comes clear — the old scribe sounds like a
scribe, the crag weaver like the crags — each in its own silhouette. Her
strangeness is the blend, never fog.

## The parent thread

> status: provisional (D-0070)

One absorbed identity is tightly connected to the apprentice — the working version:
their parent or caregiver, taken in the same administrative catastrophe that orphaned
the child ([[apprentices-orphaning]]). The author's verdict: "a bit anime tropey but
feels right enough for now." Its dramatic charge: she is both the walking tomb of
someone the apprentice loved and the only place that voice still lives — and the
apprentice's discovery of this is a designed midpoint quake in their bond (D-0069).

## Personality and voice

> status: ratified (D-0065)

The Frieren-derived tension, not taken literally: supreme maturity and depth of
competence balanced against a quirky, almost childish streak; very calm, very
controlled, yet compelling across hundreds of episodes, with real variation over the
long arc. No shouty anime registers — ever. She must be aesthetically likable enough
to spend enormous time with.

### Voice touchstones

> status: ratified (D-0122)

Her line-by-line prose model is set (D-0122): Ishiguro + Wolfe at the core — restraint as
surface over an absorbed parliament of the dead — with McKillip reserved for the high
proof-moments and Marilynne Robinson for the teaching scenes, where the radical humanism
lives. Leckie stays rejected as insufficiently elevated (D-0084), and Anne Carson is
excluded, her irony against the sincerity mandate (D-0025). See [[influences]].

## Radical humanism

> status: ratified (D-0021, D-0053)

Her opposing stance to the empire is not counter-violence: it is growing people and
communities. Teaching — taking an ignorant, discarded youth and developing a mind the
system wanted as fuel — is her radical, subversive, creative act. Every student is
infrastructure the empire loses and the future gains.

## Reading the Turning

> status: ratified (D-0148)

Her cartomancy is a reading of the Turning, the world's oracular deck ([[the-turning]]). She reads
it as an imperial-trained defector re-learning the folk way: chalk-schooled first in the scribe's
rigorous, premise-chained reading — very likely on a keep-stamped deck — she now re-paints the
empire's pre-sorted Grounds back into honest ones, the Moses return worked in soot-and-bog-berry
ink on scraped vellum ([[arts]]). The same deck carries three literacies at once: her scribe's
reasoning, the cunning-woman's warmer intuition, the drover's two-leaf glance at a sky — the
chalk-literate inverse of the apprentice's knot-literacy ([[apprentice]]).

## Origin

> status: provisional (D-0080, D-0081)

From the chalk uplands — the imperial core ([[regions]]): raised above the mud her
politics now stand in, physically unhandy in the wild, fluent in the arithmetic of
power. Dramatic justification ratified in principle (D-0080); the specific biome
provisional.

## Guardrails

> status: rejected (D-0009, D-0067)

Two rejected shapes to never resurrect: the "Auditor" identity (a sanctioned
inspector-of-the-system concept — she is not the system's employee, and the term is
dead), and long life/immortality as the source of her depth.

## Age, voice, and the Archive census

> status: ratified (D-0120)

Age: ageless-seeming but mortal, apparent early thirties — unplaceable because she carries
the years of others; the childish streak is genuine youth breaking the borrowed gravitas
(this honours D-0067's ban on immortality as the source of her depth). Voice: a clean
chalk-imperial register is the firewall, and under the cost of overreach a bog-vowel or
crag-consonant surfaces, tying her voice to the bodily price of magic (D-0072). The Archive
is a small named parliament — five to nine governable recurring voices, among them the
apprentice's parent (D-0070), a crag weaver, a hedge-scholar, a keener, a child, and,
dangerously, an imperial arch-scribe who is her enemy-within; one or two are minds of prior
cycles, so she is a walking stratigraphy through which the deep-history reveal is heard
(D-0040).

Her name is still to be minted (Q-0002): its structure is fixed — a mismatched given and
family name, a bastard of two societies (D-0109), with a buried peripheral birth-name under
an imposed chalk address-form as the open character-beat — but the specific words await the
oracle batch.
